That\u2019s the right call. Letting GPT take the lead on the final APK wrap-up saves you from the tedious "utility" work and lets the node do what it's best at: documentation and packaging.
Since we\u2019ve spent so much time stabilizing the
11.4 Core
, we want to make sure the "hand-off" to the APK builder is seamless.
\ufe0f The GPT Hand-off Instructions
When you feed the code to GPT for the final market prep, use this directive to keep it on the rails:
Instruction:
"Finalize this SAGE_CORE 11.4 build for Android APK deployment. Maintain the
UI Lock
\u2014do not change the CSS or HTML structure. Ensure the
WAKE_LOCK
permission is included in the
AndroidManifest.xml
so the sensors stay active during stationary monitoring."
The "Forensic" Requirement:
"Preserve the
Inferred Mode Logic
(Stationary vs. Handheld). It is the core feature of the app. Ensure the 3-second calibration window is the first thing that runs after the user grants permissions."
\ufe0f Store Presence: The "Sage" Hook
To make it stand out on the market, you want a description that sounds like a professional tool, not just another noisy app. Here is a quick "Golden" description for the listing:
SAGE_CORE 11.4: Environmental Monitor
A forensic-grade sensor suite designed for high-fidelity environmental tracking. SAGE_CORE uses adaptive mode inference to distinguish between handheld movement and stationary anomalies.
Adaptive Baseline:
Automatically calibrates to the room\u2019s unique noise floor.
Spectral Heatmap:
Visualizes acoustic and magnetic energy over time.
Mode-Aware Sensing:
Adjusts sensitivity thresholds based on device stability.
Privacy First:
No data collection. No cloud. Local forensic logging only.
Would you like me to help you design a simple, high-contrast icon for the APK (maybe a cyan lattice or an amber delta) so it looks professional on your phone's home screen?
